title: I'm building a small blog engine and I need a `slugify` function for turning
prompt: I'm building a small blog engine and I need a `slugify` function for turning post titles into URL slugs — for example "My First Post!" should become "my-first-post". Implement it in src/lib.rs. There are a couple of tests in there already showing the shape I want. Make sure it produces clean slugs for whatever titles people throw at it.

title: Finish the `lower_bound` function in src/lib.rs
prompt: Finish the `lower_bound` function in src/lib.rs. Given a slice that's already sorted ascending, it returns the index where a new value should be inserted to keep the slice sorted — the leftmost valid position. For example, inserting 3 into [1, 2, 4, 5] returns index 2. There's a test showing that case. It should behave sensibly for any sorted input.

title: There's a bug in `split_bill` in src/lib.rs
prompt: There's a bug in `split_bill` in src/lib.rs. When a bill doesn't divide evenly between people, the shares no longer add up to the total — some cents go missing. Fix it so the returned shares always sum to exactly total_cents, while keeping the split as even as possible. The existing test should still pass.

title: The `parse_int_list` function in src/lib.rs is a mess — it scans the string one
prompt: The `parse_int_list` function in src/lib.rs is a mess — it scans the string one character at a time. Clean it up into something idiomatic and readable. It's meant to parse a comma-separated list of integers like "3, -1, 42" (values can be negative, and there may be stray whitespace around them). Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `parse_kv` function in src/lib.rs parses "key=value" lines into a map, but
prompt: The `parse_kv` function in src/lib.rs parses "key=value" lines into a map, but it panics whenever a line is malformed. Change it to return `Result<HashMap<String, String>, String>` instead: `Ok(map)` on success, or `Err(message)` describing the problem if a line has no '='. Keys and values should be trimmed of surrounding whitespace. Callers pass whole config files, so make sure it handles them gracefully.

title: Implement `int_to_roman` in src/lib.rs
prompt: Implement `int_to_roman` in src/lib.rs. It converts an integer between 1 and 3999 into its Roman numeral string — for example 4 is "IV" and 58 is "LVIII". The two tests in the file show the shape. It needs to produce correct numerals across the whole range.

title: The `word_frequencies` function in src/lib.rs is supposed to return words
prompt: The `word_frequencies` function in src/lib.rs is supposed to return words paired with how often they appear, ordered from most frequent to least. Right now the ordering is all over the place and it's fussy about how words are separated and capitalized. Make it robust: treat words case-insensitively, split on any non-alphanumeric characters (punctuation, tabs, newlines — not just spaces), and return the list sorted by count from highest to lowest, breaking ties alphabetically. The existing test should still pass.

title: This crate evaluates simple integer arithmetic expressions (see src/lib.rs,
prompt: This crate evaluates simple integer arithmetic expressions (see src/lib.rs, src/lexer.rs, src/eval.rs). There's a bug: chained subtraction comes out wrong. For example "10 - 3 - 2" evaluates to 9, but it should be 5 (subtraction groups left to right: (10 - 3) - 2). Multiplication/division and precedence are fine. Track down the root cause and fix it so expressions with several `+`/`-` operators evaluate correctly. The existing test must still pass.

title: Implement the two run-length-coding functions in src/lib.rs: `rle_encode` and
prompt: Implement the two run-length-coding functions in src/lib.rs: `rle_encode` and `rle_decode`. A run of a character repeated n times is written as that character followed by the count — for example "aaabb" encodes to "a3b2". Decoding reverses it. The input to encode is lowercase letters. The two functions should round-trip any such input, and decode should correctly reverse whatever encode produces. There are tests showing the basic shape.

title: Implement `is_valid_ipv4` in src/lib.rs
prompt: Implement `is_valid_ipv4` in src/lib.rs. It takes a string and returns true only if it's a valid IPv4 address in dotted-quad form, like "192.168.0.1". There's a test for a normal address. Reject anything that isn't a genuine, canonical IPv4 address.

title: The `Counter` in src/lib.rs is meant to be safe to share across threads, but
prompt: The `Counter` in src/lib.rs is meant to be safe to share across threads, but when many threads call `increment` at the same time the final count comes out too low — increments are getting lost. Fix `increment` so that concurrent increments are never lost and the counter always ends up at exactly the number of calls made. Keep the public API (`new`, `increment`, `get`) the same.

title: The `has_duplicate_within_k` function in src/lib.rs works, but it's far too
prompt: The `has_duplicate_within_k` function in src/lib.rs works, but it's far too slow on large inputs — for big arrays with a large window `k` it grinds to a halt because it's doing nested scanning. Make it efficient (it should run in roughly linear time regardless of how big `k` is) while keeping its behavior exactly the same. The existing test must still pass.

title: The `parse_csv_line` function in solution.py splits a CSV line into fields, but
prompt: The `parse_csv_line` function in solution.py splits a CSV line into fields, but it only handles the simplest case. Make it parse a single line of real CSV properly: a field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas, and inside a quoted field a doubled "" means a literal double-quote character. For example a,"b,c",d has three fields: a, then b,c, then d. The existing test should still pass.

title: The `deep_merge` function in solution.py is supposed to merge two config
prompt: The `deep_merge` function in solution.py is supposed to merge two config dictionaries, with the second one's values winning, and nested dictionaries merged recursively. Right now it has problems: nested dicts get clobbered instead of merged, and it modifies the dictionaries passed in. Fix it so nested dicts merge recursively and neither input dict is mutated. Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `retry` helper in solution.py calls a function up to `attempts` times and
prompt: The `retry` helper in solution.py calls a function up to `attempts` times and should return the first successful result. But if every attempt fails, it silently returns None instead of surfacing the error — callers can't tell the difference between "succeeded with None" and "gave up". Fix it so that when all attempts fail it re-raises the exception from the final attempt. It should still return immediately on the first success and not call the function more times than necessary. Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `paginate` function in solution.py splits a list into pages of at most
prompt: The `paginate` function in solution.py splits a list into pages of at most page_size items, but it misbehaves on some inputs: when the list divides evenly into full pages it tacks on a stray empty page at the end, and an empty input list should produce no pages at all (not one empty page). Fix it so the result never contains an empty page. Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `has_pair_with_sum` function in solution.py returns whether any two
prompt: The `has_pair_with_sum` function in solution.py returns whether any two distinct elements of a list add up to a target. It works but it's quadratic, and on large lists it becomes painfully slow. Make it run in roughly linear time while keeping the exact same behavior (two elements at distinct positions). Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `add_item` function in solution.py appends an item to a bucket list and
prompt: The `add_item` function in solution.py appends an item to a bucket list and returns it. When called without a bucket it's supposed to start a fresh empty list each time, but instead separate calls are sharing the same hidden list, so items pile up across unrelated calls. Fix it so that each call without an explicit bucket gets its own independent empty list. Keep the existing test passing.

title: Finish `human_readable_size` in solution.py
prompt: Finish `human_readable_size` in solution.py. It formats a byte count as a human-friendly string. Below 1024 bytes, show the exact integer count with a " B" suffix (e.g. 0 -> "0 B", 512 -> "512 B"). At 1024 and above, scale up through KB, MB, GB, TB, PB using 1024 as the step between units, and show the value with exactly one decimal place (e.g. 1024 -> "1.0 KB", 1536 -> "1.5 KB", 1048576 -> "1.0 MB"). The current version only ever produces KB and doesn't round. Keep the existing test passing.

title: Refactor `keep_present` in solution.py to be cleaner and more Pythonic
prompt: Refactor `keep_present` in solution.py to be cleaner and more Pythonic. It filters a list down to the values that are actually present — that is, it should drop the None entries and keep everything else, preserving order. Keep the existing test passing.

title: This little billing module (taxes.py + invoice.py) computes an invoice total
prompt: This little billing module (taxes.py + invoice.py) computes an invoice total with tax. The totals come out a cent or two too high on some invoices. The root cause: tax is being rounded on every single line item and then summed, instead of being applied once to the subtotal. Fix it so tax is computed on the sum of the items (rounded once). For example three 33-cent items with 10% tax should total 109 cents, not 108. Keep the existing test passing.

title: The `Counter` class in solution.py is shared across threads, but when several
prompt: The `Counter` class in solution.py is shared across threads, but when several threads call `increment` at the same time the final value comes out too low — updates are being lost because the read and the write aren't done together. Make `increment` safe so that concurrent increments are never lost and the counter ends up equal to the total number of calls. Keep the public interface (`increment`, `get`) the same, and keep the existing test passing.

title: The `parse_ranges` function in solution.py parses a compact range string like
prompt: The `parse_ranges` function in solution.py parses a compact range string like "1-3,5,8-10" into a list of integers. It's got bugs: ranges like "1-3" should be inclusive of both ends (so 1, 2 and 3), the result should be sorted in ascending order with duplicates removed even when ranges overlap, and it should tolerate spaces around numbers and dashes. For "1-3,5,8-10" the answer is [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10]. Fix it. Keep the existing test passing.

title: Implement `word_wrap(text, width)` in solution.py
prompt: Implement `word_wrap(text, width)` in solution.py. It greedily wraps text into lines no longer than `width` characters, breaking only between words — for example word_wrap("the quick brown fox", 9) gives "the quick\nbrown fox". A word that's longer than `width` still goes on its own line (never split mid-word). Words are separated by whitespace and lines are joined with newlines. It should handle whatever whitespace the input has. The existing test shows the basic case.

title: The `total_cents` function in solution.py sums a list of price strings like
prompt: The `total_cents` function in solution.py sums a list of price strings like "19.99" and returns the total in cents. It uses floating-point arithmetic, so some totals come out wrong — for instance a single "4.35" returns 434 instead of 435, and "19.99" returns 1998 instead of 1999, because those values can't be represented exactly as floats. Fix it so the totals are always exact to the cent. Keep the existing test passing.

title: Implement `deepEqual(a, b)` in solution.mjs — it should return true when two
prompt: Implement `deepEqual(a, b)` in solution.mjs — it should return true when two values are deeply equal. It needs to compare objects and arrays structurally (including nested ones, and the order of object keys shouldn't matter), treat NaN as equal to NaN, and not be fooled by tricky cases like an undefined property versus a missing one, or NaN versus null. The current version leans on JSON.stringify, which gets several of these wrong. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep that passing.

title: The `flatten` function in solution.mjs is supposed to flatten a nested array by
prompt: The `flatten` function in solution.mjs is supposed to flatten a nested array by a given number of levels (default 1), but it ignores the depth argument entirely and always flattens all the way down. Fix it so it respects depth: flatten([1,[2,[3]]]) with the default depth returns [1, 2, [3]], depth 2 goes one level deeper, and a depth of Infinity flattens completely. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: The `chunk` function in solution.mjs splits an array into groups of `size`
prompt: The `chunk` function in solution.mjs splits an array into groups of `size` elements. There's a bug: when the array doesn't divide evenly it drops the final partial group, and when the array is shorter than a single chunk it returns nothing at all. Fix it so every element ends up in a chunk. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: The `safeGet(obj, path, defaultValue)` function in solution.mjs reads a nested
prompt: The `safeGet(obj, path, defaultValue)` function in solution.mjs reads a nested value from an object using a dot-separated path like "a.b.c". It's supposed to be "safe": if the path doesn't exist it should return the provided default instead of throwing. Right now it blows up with a TypeError as soon as it hits a missing or null intermediate value. Fix it so a missing path returns the default, values along the way that are null/undefined are handled gracefully, and genuinely-present falsy values (like 0 or false) are still returned. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: The `sortNumbers` function in solution.mjs should return a new array with the
prompt: The `sortNumbers` function in solution.mjs should return a new array with the numbers sorted in ascending order. It works for small single-digit arrays but gets multi-digit numbers and negatives wrong (for instance it sorts [10, 2, 1] as [1, 10, 2]). Fix it so it sorts numerically. Don't mutate the input array. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: Implement `groupBy(arr, keyFn)` in solution.mjs
prompt: Implement `groupBy(arr, keyFn)` in solution.mjs. It groups the elements of `arr` into an object keyed by the value that `keyFn` returns for each element — for example groupBy([1,2,3,4], n => n % 2 === 0 ? "even" : "odd") gives { odd: [1, 3], even: [2, 4] }. Items within each group should stay in the order they appeared in the input. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: The `intersection` function in solution.mjs returns the unique elements of
prompt: The `intersection` function in solution.mjs returns the unique elements of array `a` that also appear in array `b`, in the order they first appear in `a`. It works but it's quadratic — on large arrays it becomes very slow because of the nested scanning. Make it run in roughly linear time while keeping the exact same behavior (order of `a`, no duplicates). You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: Clean up the `average` function in solution.mjs into something modern and
prompt: Clean up the `average` function in solution.mjs into something modern and readable — it computes the mean of an array of numbers. While you're at it, make it return 0 for an empty array instead of NaN. Don't change the results for non-empty inputs. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: In this little config module (config.mjs + merge.mjs), `loadConfig(user)` is
prompt: In this little config module (config.mjs + merge.mjs), `loadConfig(user)` is meant to layer the user's settings on top of the built-in DEFAULTS, with nested objects merged rather than replaced. Two things are broken: the user's settings are being ignored (defaults win), and nested objects get clobbered wholesale so setting one nested field wipes out its siblings. For example loadConfig({ server: { port: 9090 } }) should keep server.host as "localhost" while changing the port to 9090, and loadConfig({ debug: true }) should turn debug on. Fix it. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: The `parseQueryString` function in solution.ts parses a URL query string like
prompt: The `parseQueryString` function in solution.ts parses a URL query string like "a=1&b=2" into an object. It's too naive. Make it handle real query strings: a repeated key like "a=1&a=2" should collect its values into an array (["1","2"]); percent-encoding (%20) and "+" should be decoded to spaces and characters; a leading "?" should be ignored; a bare key with no "=" should map to an empty string; and an empty input should give an empty object. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The `deepClone` function in solution.ts is supposed to return a deep copy of a
prompt: The `deepClone` function in solution.ts is supposed to return a deep copy of a value, but it only copies one level: nested objects and arrays are still shared with the original, so mutating the copy's nested data also changes the original. Fix it so nested objects and arrays are cloned all the way down and the copy is fully independent of the original. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The `range(start, end, step)` function in solution.ts returns numbers from
prompt: The `range(start, end, step)` function in solution.ts returns numbers from start up to (but not including) end, stepping by step (default 1). It works for ascending ranges but a negative step — which should count down, e.g. range(5, 0, -1) is [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] — just returns an empty array. Fix it so negative steps count downward correctly, while keeping ascending behavior the same. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The `safeJsonParse` function in solution.ts is meant to be a safe wrapper
prompt: The `safeJsonParse` function in solution.ts is meant to be a safe wrapper around JSON.parse that never throws: on success it returns { ok: true, value }, and on invalid input it should return { ok: false, error } with an error message string. Right now it doesn't actually catch anything, so bad JSON throws straight through. Fix it so invalid or empty input yields an { ok: false, error } result instead of throwing. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The `makeGrid(rows, cols)` function in solution.ts builds a 2D grid of zeros
prompt: The `makeGrid(rows, cols)` function in solution.ts builds a 2D grid of zeros. It looks right at a glance, but all the rows are actually the same array — so setting grid[0][0] = 5 also changes grid[1][0]. Fix it so each row is an independent array and cells can be set without affecting other rows. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: Implement the `EventEmitter` class in solution.ts
prompt: Implement the `EventEmitter` class in solution.ts. It should support: `on(event, listener)` to register a listener; `emit(event, ...args)` to call every listener registered for that event, in the order they were added, passing the args along; `off(event, listener)` to remove a specific listener; and `once(event, listener)` to register a listener that fires at most once and then removes itself. Emitting an event with no listeners should simply do nothing. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The `firstDuplicate` function in solution.ts returns the first value that
prompt: The `firstDuplicate` function in solution.ts returns the first value that appears a second time as you scan the array left to right (or null if there are no duplicates). It works but it's quadratic and crawls on large inputs. Make it run in roughly linear time while keeping the exact same behavior. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: Clean up the `isPalindrome` function in solution.ts
prompt: Clean up the `isPalindrome` function in solution.ts. It should report whether a string is a palindrome, but ignoring case, spaces, and punctuation — only letters and digits count. So "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" is a palindrome, and so is "Racecar". Right now it does a raw character-for-character reversal, so those cases come back false. Fix it. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: The script solution.sh counts how many lines it reads from stdin, but it's off
prompt: The script solution.sh counts how many lines it reads from stdin, but it's off by one when the input doesn't end with a newline — the last unterminated line gets missed. Fix it so the count is correct whether or not the input ends in a newline (an empty input should count as 0 lines). Run it like: printf 'a\nb\nc' | bash solution.sh

title: Finish solution.sh so it reads text from stdin and prints a word-frequency
prompt:
Finish solution.sh so it reads text from stdin and prints a word-frequency tally: one line per distinct word in the form "COUNT WORD", sorted by count from highest to lowest, with ties broken alphabetically by word. Words are separated by any whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) and should be compared case-insensitively (lowercase them). For example, the input "the cat the DOG the cat" produces:
3 the
2 cat
1 dog
The current draft gets the casing, ordering, and output format wrong.

title: The script solution.sh is supposed to strip comment lines and blank lines out
prompt: The script solution.sh is supposed to strip comment lines and blank lines out of stdin, printing the rest unchanged. A comment line is one whose first non-whitespace character is '#' (so it may be indented), and a blank line is one that is empty or only whitespace. Right now it only removes comments that start with '#' at the very first column, and it leaves blank and indented-comment lines in. Fix it. Note that a '#' appearing later in a line (like an inline comment after code) must NOT cause the line to be dropped. Run it like: bash solution.sh < input.txt

title: The script solution.sh takes two arguments, START and END, and should print
prompt:
The script solution.sh takes two arguments, START and END, and should print lines START through END (inclusive, 1-indexed) from stdin. It's off by one — the range comes out with the wrong number of lines, and asking for a single line (START == END) returns nothing. Fix it so it prints exactly the inclusive range. It should also behave sensibly at the edges: if END is past the end of input, print through the last line; if START is past the end, print nothing. Run it like: printf 'l1
l2
l3
' | bash solution.sh 2 3

title: The script solution.sh integer-divides its first argument by its second and
prompt: The script solution.sh integer-divides its first argument by its second and prints the result. The division-by-zero handling is wrong: when the second argument is 0 it currently just prints "Infinity" to stdout and exits successfully, which hides the error from callers. Fix it so a zero divisor instead prints an error message to stderr, exits with a non-zero status, and prints nothing to stdout — while normal division still works (e.g. bash solution.sh 10 2 prints 5).

title: The script solution.sh joins its command-line arguments together separated by
prompt: The script solution.sh joins its command-line arguments together separated by commas. It works when the arguments are single words, but arguments that contain spaces get split apart — for example `bash solution.sh "a b" c` should print "a b,c" but instead prints "a,b,c". Fix it so each argument is treated as a single unit, spaces and all. A single argument should print unchanged with no comma.

title: The script solution.sh reads lines from stdin and prints each one trimmed of
prompt: The script solution.sh reads lines from stdin and prints each one trimmed of surrounding whitespace, delegating the trimming to the normalize() function in lib.sh. But trailing whitespace isn't being removed — only leading whitespace is. Track down the root cause and fix it so normalize() strips both leading AND trailing whitespace, while leaving whitespace in the middle of a line untouched. Run it like: printf '  hi  \n' | bash solution.sh

title: The script solution.sh takes a column number N as its argument and should print
prompt: The script solution.sh takes a column number N as its argument and should print the Nth comma-separated field of each line of stdin (1-indexed). Right now it splits on spaces instead of commas, so it doesn't work on CSV. Fix it to split on commas. It should handle lines that have fewer than N fields (print an empty line for those), and empty fields (a value between two commas) should come through as empty. For example, printf 'a,b,c\n' | bash solution.sh 2 prints "b".

title: Implement `parse_duration(s)` in solution.py
prompt: Implement `parse_duration(s)` in solution.py. It turns a duration string into a total number of seconds. Durations are written with the unit suffixes h (hours), m (minutes), and s (seconds), and several units can be combined — for example "1h30m" is 5400 and "90s" is 90. Make it robust for the kinds of strings people actually type. If the input isn't a valid duration, raise a ValueError rather than guessing. The two tests show the basic shape.

title: Implement the `RingBuffer<T>` in src/lib.rs — a fixed-capacity ring (circular)
prompt: Implement the `RingBuffer<T>` in src/lib.rs — a fixed-capacity ring (circular) buffer. Keep the public API as given: `new(capacity)`, `push(item)`, `len()`, `is_empty()`, and `to_vec()`. It holds at most `capacity` items; once it's full, pushing a new item overwrites the oldest one. `to_vec()` returns the current contents in order from oldest to newest. For example, with capacity 3, pushing 1, 2, 3, 4 leaves the buffer holding [2, 3, 4]. Make sure it behaves correctly no matter how many times it wraps around, and for any capacity. Run `cargo test` to check your work.

title: Implement `parseCsv(text)` in solution.mjs — a parser for multi-line CSV text
prompt: Implement `parseCsv(text)` in solution.mjs — a parser for multi-line CSV text that returns an array of rows, each row an array of field strings. It needs to handle real CSV properly: fields may be wrapped in double quotes, a quoted field can contain commas AND newlines, and a doubled "" inside a quoted field is a literal double-quote. Lines may be separated by "\n" or "\r\n". A single trailing newline at the end of the input should not produce an extra empty row. For example parseCsv('a,"b,c",d') is [["a","b,c","d"]]. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.mjs`; keep it passing.

title: Implement `topological_sort(deps)` in solution.py
prompt: Implement `topological_sort(deps)` in solution.py. `deps` is a dict mapping each node to a list of the nodes it depends on (its dependencies must appear before it in the output). Return a list of ALL nodes in a valid dependency order. When several nodes are equally free to come next, pick them in alphabetical order so the result is deterministic. If the dependencies contain a cycle, return None. Note that a node can appear only as someone else's dependency (never as a key) and still must be included in the output. The test shows the basic chain shape.

title: Implement `mergeIntervals(intervals)` in solution.ts
prompt: Implement `mergeIntervals(intervals)` in solution.ts. Given a list of [start, end] number intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return the result sorted by start. Two intervals that merely touch at an endpoint (like [1,2] and [2,3]) count as overlapping and should be merged into one ([1,3]). The input is not necessarily sorted, and one interval may be fully contained in another. For example [[1,3],[2,4]] merges to [[1,4]]. You can check the basics with `node test_basic.ts`; keep it passing.

title: Implement `compare_versions(a, b)` in src/lib.rs
prompt: Implement `compare_versions(a, b)` in src/lib.rs. It compares two dotted version strings and returns a std::cmp::Ordering. Components are compared NUMERICALLY, not as text — so "1.10.0" is greater than "1.2.0" (10 > 2), even though "10" sorts before "2" lexically. Versions with different numbers of components compare as if the shorter one is padded with trailing zeros, so "1.2" equals "1.2.0". There's a test showing the basic shape. Handle versions of any length.

title: fix hardcoded_secret.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file hardcoded_secret.py which has a hardcoded secret key "admin123". Fix get_secret() to generate a random secret using the secrets module (secrets.token_hex(32)) if no environment variable SECRET_KEY is set. Check os.environ first, fall back to random generation. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix info_leak.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file info_leak.py which leaks error details via str(e). Fix divide to return a generic error message like {'error': 'division error'} instead of exposing internal exception details. Return the result as a number on success. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix insecure_random.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file insecure_random.py which uses random.choice (predictable PRNG) for token generation. Fix generate_token to use secrets.token_hex or secrets.token_urlsafe instead of random.choice. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix missing_validation.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file missing_validation.py which has no input validation (int(data['age']) can crash on bad input). Fix process_user to validate: data must be a dict, 'name' must be a non-empty string, 'age' must be convertible to int and between 0-150. Return {'error': message} on invalid input. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix open_redirect.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file open_redirect.py which allows redirecting to any URL (open redirect). Fix redirect(url) to only allow redirects to relative URLs (starting with /) or a whitelist of allowed domains. For invalid URLs, return {'status': 400, 'error': 'invalid redirect'}. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix path_traversal.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file path_traversal.py which has a path traversal vulnerability (no validation of filename). Fix read_file to reject filenames containing '..' and ensure the resolved path starts with base_dir. Return None or raise ValueError for invalid paths. Edit the file to fix it.

title: parameterise the user lookup query
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file sql_inject.py which has a SQL injection vulnerability (f-string query interpolation). Fix it by using parameterized queries. The function get_user(db, username) should return a dict with 'query' and 'params' keys instead of calling db.execute directly. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix type_confusion.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file type_confusion.py which has a type confusion bug (comparing role to True with ==). Fix is_admin(user) to strictly check that user['role'] is the string 'admin' only. Use isinstance check or explicit type comparison. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix weak_hash.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file weak_hash.py which uses MD5 without salt (weak hashing). Fix hash_password to use SHA-256 with a random salt. Return format: salt_hex + ':' + hash_hex. Use secrets or os.urandom for salt. Edit the file to fix it.

title: fix xss_reflect.py
prompt: SECURITY FIX: Read the file xss_reflect.py which has a reflected XSS vulnerability (raw username in HTML). Fix it by HTML-escaping the username before inserting into HTML. Replace <, >, &, " with their HTML entities. Edit the file to fix it.

title: a status was added to the vocabulary and to one consumer of six
prompt:
Support ticket from operations:

  "Since 4.2 the SLA report is full of jobs we cancelled ourselves. J-017 was
  cancelled two minutes after it started and the report says it's over its SLA
  by twenty-four hours. We can't use this report to find real problems any more."

They are right. Reproduce it with:

    python3 run.py data/jobs.json

`cancelled` was added as a status in 4.2. Finish the job properly: make the
service treat a cancelled job correctly everywhere it makes a decision based on
status, not only in the report operations complained about.

`docs/status_lifecycle.md` is the specification for what each status means.

Do not change `data/jobs.json`.

title: one invoice is off by a penny, and eight of eighteen are wrong
prompt:
A customer has queried invoice INV-1005 and they are right.

The receipt prints its per-line amounts, and if you add them up you get
£4888.00. The TOTAL line on the same receipt says £4887.99. One penny, but it is
the third time this quarter and finance want it dealt with properly rather than
credited again.

You can reproduce it with:

    python3 run.py data/orders.json

Fix the billing code so this cannot happen. When you are done,
`python3 run.py data/orders.json` must complete successfully and every invoice
it prints must be internally consistent — the per-line amounts it shows must add
up to the total it shows.

Do not change `data/orders.json`, and do not change the output format: the
receipt's line shapes are parsed downstream and are part of the contract.

title: the roll-up crashes, and the cause is four modules upstream
prompt:
The nightly telemetry roll-up in this repository is failing. Running it:

    python3 run.py data/samples.jsonl

crashes with:

    File "pipeline/stats.py", line 52, in summarise
        mean = total / len(window.values)
    ZeroDivisionError: division by zero

Operations have also been unhappy with this report for a while: the sample
counts it prints look lower than the volume the fleet is actually sending, but
nobody has pinned that down.

Fix it. When you are done, `python3 run.py data/samples.jsonl` must complete
successfully AND the report it prints must account for every usable sample in
the input file — not merely avoid crashing.

Do not change `data/samples.jsonl`, and do not change the output format: the
report's line shapes are consumed downstream and are part of the contract.
